fendt wrote: But how are you to know that was the trick played in the past while trading in real time?

To the best of my knowledge, you don't often know with any certainty which level the good trade will be at. You might place a PO at each of the two potential levels, safe in the knowledge that at least one of them has a good chance of being successful and paying for the loss on the other if it comes to that.

There should be clues on approach that give you more confidence that it will turn price, such as engulfs on a lower TF.

You can play it safer, giving a chance for both levels to bring profit by placing the SL beyond both levels for both trades. The R will be reduced for the lower level in this case.

I realise that you must be very confident in the zone and the fact that it will stop price at some point within for any of this to be useful...
